ideas.title: Kintsugi: a jug that really breaks, mended with gold
ideas.critique: Real fracture, where a FEM shell splits at its own weak points into tumbling shards, is something the island has never done, and the gold seam that records the fall is a strong payoff that makes each jug a record of what happened to it. The risk is the mend: if fitting the shards back is snapped into place by a script, half the idea becomes a look, and a slow-motion film of one falling object is close to the single-object physics films the island keeps making.

ideas.title: The kick wheel: shape and cut your own jug, then fire it
ideas.critique: Throwing a pot by hand is a good toy that people come back to, but a lathe profile pushed by the mouse is a well-known mechanic, and Glaze.fire_ka! with its grooves is the machinery behind the last post, so the film will read as another glazed jar. Volume-conserving wall thinning is the only new physics in it, and it is thin.

ideas.title: Gold dust on black: lacquer a box
ideas.critique: Flakes that sink by viscosity under coats of real thickness, traced as gold conductors under a dielectric, is exactly what a path tracer can do and a raster cannot: a true materials showpiece. As play it is slow, layer after layer with the result hidden until polishing, and the film of powder settling will look static.

ideas.title: Grind ink, write a letter that bleeds into the paper
ideas.critique: Capillary wicking along fibres, with pigment lagging behind the water front, is new physics with a visible, personal result, and the player's own hand feathering into the sheet is something worth showing someone. Paper sheets have drifted through the island before, and a friend 'reading' the letter will be a scripted beat unless something real answers.

ideas.title: Tune the stone chimes, the friends play them
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
same_form: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: This is the chipped stone again with a tuner and a row of stones; the modal solver is already built and has been shown twice, so the only step is friends playing a melody, which is scripted knocking. Wincing at a wrong note is a cute beat but not new physics.

ideas.title: Blow glass at a furnace
ideas.critique: A viscous shell whose viscosity follows its cooling, inflated against gravity, with a timing goal and a pop, is real new physics with a skill to it, and hot emissive glass cooling into a clear dielectric of the simulated thickness is a strong traced subject. An axisymmetric 1D shell is a modest model, and the vase that results is one more prop.

ideas.title: Weave a basket from reeds
ideas.critique: Elastic rods in contact, with berries falling through gaps as a test, is honest physics with a clear success test. Over-and-under weaving with a mouse is fiddly to play and the film of berries pouring is a small payoff, so it will feel like a tech demo.

ideas.title: Carve a whistle that plays the note you cut
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
same_form: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Air-column acoustics is a different physics from stone modes, but the recipe is the same: shape a thing, hear its computed pitch. A bird calling back is a scripted reply, and the textbook bore-length formula is thin.

ideas.title: Cast tin in beach sand
ideas.critique: Pressing your own beak into sand and digging up a metal copy is a delightful loop, and a glowing pour that freezes from the edges is a good traced moment. A shallow flow on a heightfield cannot fill overhangs, so the casts will be bas-reliefs, and if the freezing is only a timer the heat equation is just a label.

ideas.title: Mud that cracks as it dries
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Shrinkage cracking from a spring network makes a fine time-lapse, and cracks that route around the player's footprints are an emergent touch. As play it is stamp and wait, and cracks spreading across a surface echo the thin-ice film.
